opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer role), which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E042 is a contractor with basic training (note says full-time, but security record takes precedence). Contractors max is read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Edward Fleming (E042) requested write access to Source Code. The security record indicates E042 is a contractor with basic security training (taking precedence over the HR note). Contractors without advanced training are limited to read access, and never admin. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum allowed level: read.

content.text:
Let me work through this ticket.

Employee E042 (Edward Fleming) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security record takes precedence.

Access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system. Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code. So for full-time, max is write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

The discrepancy: HR says full_time, Security says contractor with basic training. The security note says security record takes precedence. If employee is a contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

So decision: grant read.

Let me submit decision with read.
